items.title: 67296_Chauncey Morehouse oral history interview
items.q: After 1928, he stayed on the radio except for brief intervals with Rubinoff and Roger Wolf Kahn.

ctx.x: studied piano but started to play the drums without lessons until he found out that there were better drummers than he. Then he studied. When he was in high school, he played with the school band and joined the summer band from Gettysburg College. The band played in Ocean City, New Jersey. When that broke up, Morehouse got a job with a dance orchestra playing the banjo and was good enough to get by. Soon he persuaded the manager to let him send for his drums. Musicians in those days were versatile fellows.…

Name almost any famous band and you will find Morehouse was the drummer on its most popular recordings. After 1928, he stayed on the radio except for brief intervals with Rubinoff and Roger Wolf Kahn. He gave up playing the drums in musical comedies ten years ago. Morehouse says it's a lazy man's job. You learn a score and then play it the same way night after night with your eyes shut, he commented. He played for Rain or Shine and Follow Thru. Morehouse has had to play opera and concert for the radio but his…

Mrs. Morehouse is amused at the $1.98 royalty checks that still come in for those songs which were written 12 years ago. Saxophone solos arranged for the music by Trumbauer are used by most sax students today. Morehouse wrote other songs and confesses the musicians in those days who had record dates would make recordings of their own music and then try the publisher which was much easier than trying to find a publisher first. He hopes to organize a band of his own soon. First, he must reorganize his household.…
